slides.sub: One camp says wait for the Fed. The other says it's out of your hands. After 6 years in real estate, here are the 6 things on your side of the table that shape it.

slides.title: What the Fed sets
slides.body: The Fed sets a target range for the [[federal funds rate]], what banks charge each other overnight. It doesn't directly set your mortgage rate. Changes to it influence other interest rates.

slides.title: What's in your hands
items: Your [[credit score]]. Higher scores generally get lower rates.
Your down payment. A bigger one generally means a lower rate.
Your loan type: conventional, FHA, VA or USDA. Rates differ by type.
slides.source: CFPB, 7 factors that determine your rate (Oct. 2026)

slides.title: 3 more that move it
items: Loan term. Shorter terms, like 15 years, generally have lower rates than 30 years.
Rate type. A fixed rate stays the same. An adjustable rate can change.
Home price, loan amount and location. Rates can differ by state.
slides.source: CFPB, 7 factors that determine your rate (Oct. 2026)

slides.title: Do this before you shop
slides.body: Check your credit reports at AnnualCreditReport.com. You can view them free every week. Then get Loan Estimates from more than one lender and [[compare them]]. Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.

caption:
The uncomfortable truth about mortgage rates: the Fed doesn't set yours.

The Fed sets a target range for the federal funds rate, what banks charge each other overnight. Changes to it influence other interest rates. But your mortgage rate also depends on things on your side of the table: your credit score, down payment, loan type, loan term, interest rate type, home price, loan amount and home location. Check your credit reports at AnnualCreditReport.com. You can view them free every week. Then compare Loan Estimates from more than one lender.

Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.
